'''Carl Svante Janson'''<ref>Page 647 in {{cite book | last1=Graham | first1=Ronald&nbsp;L. | authorlink1=Ronald L. Graham | last2=Knuth | first2=Donald&nbsp;E. | authorlink2=Donald Knuth | last3=Patashnik | first3=Oren | authorlink3=Oren Patashnik| title=[[Concrete Mathematics|Concrete mathematics: A foundation for computer science]] | edition=Second | publisher=Addison–Wesley Publishing Company| location=Reading, MA | year=1994 | pages=xiv, 657 | isbn=0-201-55802-5 | mr=1397498 }}</ref> (born 21 May 1955) is a [[Swedish people|Swedish]] [[mathematician]]. A member of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]] since 1994, Janson has been the chaired [[Professor#Main positions 2|professor]] of mathematics at [[Uppsala University]] since 1987.

In [[mathematical analysis]], Janson has publications in [[functional analysis]] (especially [[harmonic analysis]]) and [[probability theory]]. In [[mathematical statistics]], Janson has made contributions to the theory of [[U-statistic]]s.<ref>Page 508 in {{cite book | last1=Koroljuk | first1=V. S. | last2=Borovskich | first2=Yu. V. | title=Theory of ''U''-statistics | edition=Translated by P. V. Malyshev and D. V. Malyshev from the 1989 Russian original | series=Mathematics and its Applications | volume=273 | publisher= Kluwer Academic Publishers Group | location=Dordrecht | year=1994 | pages=x, 552 | isbn=0-7923-2608-3 | mr= 1472486 }}</ref><ref>Pages 381–382 in {{cite book  |last=Borovskikh | first=Yu. V. | title=''U''-statistics in Banach spaces | publisher=VSP | location=Utrecht | year=1996 | pages=xii, 420 | isbn=90-6764-200-2 | mr=1419498 }}</ref>  In [[combinatorics]], Janson has publications in [[probabilistic combinatorics]], particularly [[random graph]]s and in the [[analysis of algorithms]]: In the study of random graphs, Janson introduced U-statistics and the [[Wassily Hoeffding|Hoeffding]] decomposition.<ref>Page xii in {{cite book  | last1=Kwapień | first1=Stanisƚaw | last2=Woyczyński | first2=Wojbor A. | title=Random series and stochastic integrals: Single and multiple |  series=Probability and its Applications | publisher=Birkhäuser Boston, Inc.| location=Boston, MA | year=1992 | pages=xvi+360 | isbn=0-8176-3572-6 | mr=1167198 }}</ref>

==Biography==
Svante Janson has already had a long career in mathematics, because he started research at a very young age.
[[File:Carleson cropped.jpg| thumb |upright|[[Lennart Carleson]] was the [[doctoral advisor|doctoral supervisor]] of Svante Janson, who received his Ph.D. on his 22nd birthday.<ref name="CV"/>  Carleson had himself received his Ph.D. when he was 22 years old.<ref name="Carleson">
{{cite journal
   | last1 = Raussen
   | first1 = Martin
   | last2= Skau
   | first2 = Christian
   | title = Interview with Abel Prize Recipient Lennart Carleson
   | journal = [[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]
   |date=February 2007
   | volume = 54
   | issue = 2
   | pages =223–229
   | url = http://www.ams.org/notices/200702/comm-carleson.pdf
   | accessdate = 2008-01-16 }}</ref>]]

===From prodigy to docent===
A [[child prodigy]] in mathematics, Janson took high-school and even university classes while in primary school. He was [[university admission|admitted]] in 1968 to [[University of Gothenburg]] at age 12. After his 1968 [[matriculation#United States|matriculation]] at Uppsala University at age 13,<ref name="CV"/> Janson obtained the following degrees in mathematics: a "candidate of philosophy" (roughly an "[[honours degree|honours]]" [[B.S. degree|B.S.]] with a thesis) at age 14 (in 1970) and a [[Ph.D.|doctor of philosophy]] at age 21–22 (in 1977). Janson's Ph.D. was awarded on his 22nd birthday.<ref name="CV">[http://www.math.uu.se/~svante/cv.html Curriculum Vitæ for Svante Janson], read 18 december 2009</ref> Janson's [[doctoral dissertation]] was [[doctoral advisor|supervised]] by [[Lennart Carleson]],<ref>{{cite book | last=Janson | first=Svante | title=On BMO and related spaces | year=1977 | publisher=Department of Mathematics, Uppsala University|location=Uppsala}}</ref> who had himself received his doctoral degree when he was 22 years old.<ref name="Carleson2">
his thesis studied [[harmonic analysis]], particularly [[Hardy space]]s of [[bounded mean oscillation]] (BMO), and {{cite journal
   | last1 = Raussen
   | first1 = Martin
   | last2= Skau
   | first2 = Christian
   | title = Interview with Abel Prize Recipient Lennart Carleson
   | journal = [[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]
   |date=February 2007
   | volume = 54
   | issue = 2
   | pages =223–229
   | url = http://www.ams.org/notices/200702/comm-carleson.pdf
   | accessdate = 2008-01-16 }}</ref>

After having earned his doctorate, Janson was a [[postdoc]] with the [[Mittag-Leffler Institute]] from 1978 to 1980. Thereafter he worked at Uppsala University. Janson's ongoing research earned him another PhD from Uppsala University in 1984 – this second doctoral degree being in [[mathematical statistics]];<ref>{{cite book | last=Janson | first=Svante | title=Random coverings and related problems | year=1984 | location=Uppsala}}</ref> the  [[doctoral advisor|supervisor]] was [[Carl-Gustav Esseen]].<ref>[http://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=19988 The Mathematics Genealogy Project: Svante Janson], read 1 May 2010</ref>

In 1984, Janson was hired by [[Stockholm University]] as [[Docent#Northern Europe|docent]] (roughly [[associate professor]] in the USA).<ref name="CV"/>

===Professorships===
In 1985 Janson returned to Uppsala University, where he was named [[Professor#Main positions 2|the chaired professor]] in [[mathematical statistics]]. In 1987 Janson became [[Professor#Main positions 2|the chaired professor]] of mathematics at Uppsala university.<ref name="CV"/> Traditionally in Sweden, the ''chaired professor'' has had the role of a "''[[Professor#Main positions 2|professor ordinarius]]''" in a [[German university]] (roughly combining the roles of research professor and director of graduate studies at a [[research university]] in the USA).

==Awards==
Besides being a member of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]] (KVA), Svante Janson is a member of the [[Royal Society of Sciences in Uppsala]]. His thesis received the 1978 Sparre Award from the KVA. He received the 1994 Swedish medal for the best young mathematical scientist, the [[Göran Gustafsson Prize]]. Janson's former [[doctoral advisor|doctoral student]], Ola Hössjer, received the Göran Gustafsson prize in 2009, becoming the first [[statistician]] so honored.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.gustafssonsstiftelse.se/kva/tidigare.html | title=Göran Gustafsson prize awarded to Svante Janson in 1994 (and to Janson's student Ola Hössjer in 2009) | date=2010-06-28 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://archive.today/20120804074015/http://www.gustafssonsstiftelse.se/kva/tidigare.html | archive-date=2012-08-04 }}</ref>

In December 2009, Janson received the [[Lars Gårding|Eva & Lars Gårding]] prize from the [[Royal Physiographic Society in Lund]].<ref name="CV"/>
In 2021, Janson received the [[Flajolet Lecture Prize]].  He delivered the fifth Flajolet Lecture at the 2022 [[AofA—International Meeting on Combinatorial, Probabilistic, and Asymptotic Methods in the Analysis of Algorithms|AofA]] conference.<ref>{{cite web|title=AofA 2022, June 20–24, 2022, Philadelphia, PA, USA |url=https://drops.dagstuhl.de/storage/00lipics/lipics-vol225-aofa2022/LIPIcs.AofA.2022.0/LIPIcs.AofA.2022.0.pdf}}</ref>
